div.div: مُوَسْوِسٌ , with kesr, A man subject to وَسَاوِس [or diabolical promptings, or suggestions, of vain, or unprofitable, things, and thereby confused in his intellect, or disordered in his mind]: (M:) an act. part. n., applied as an epithet to a man, because he to whom it is applied talks to himself: and one also says مُوَسْوَسٌ, [or مُوَسْوَسٌ إِلَيْهِ,] like المَغْضُوبُ عَلَيْهِمْ: (Msb.) or, accord. to IAar, one should not say مُوَسْوَسٌ. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
